# kOA-Linux Operating System

> Sovereign, local-first, offline-capable, and governable operating system for kOA ecosystem workloads.

**Documentation architecture:** contract-first  
**Status:** normative target architecture; implementation validation required  
**Last documentation validation:** August 6, 2026

## Overview

kOA-Linux Operating System provides a governed local execution environment for knowledge, coordination, media, language, navigation, publication, recovery, and offline operation.

kOA Spaces is the optional, replaceable global experience layer. It composes validated navigation and presentation contributions into the module selector, active-module sidebar, top bar, and shared page surface. It does not own business authority, authorization, workflows, subsystem data, host privilege, resource admission, release activation, backup, or recovery.

It is not a general-purpose desktop distribution, and it does not absorb the internal authority of the applications and independently documented systems it hosts or integrates.

The repository defines:

- constitutional and system invariants;
- deployment profiles and resource envelopes;
- internal kOA components;
- trust, identity, storage, network, lifecycle, security, and operations rules;
- integration boundaries for independent systems and external services;
- release, recovery, conformance, and validation requirements.

## Core statement

> kOA-Linux owns the local operating boundary. Each component or independent system owns its declared domain. kOA Spaces owns only the optional global presentation and navigation frame. The kOA Mediatheque is the private offline media authority. UCKK is the online Moodle learning and dissemination platform. Interface composition and controlled interchange never merge authority.

## Authority model

1. Source contracts and normative source documents define current facts.
2. Accepted decisions close architectural choices.
3. Executable validators enforce declared structural and semantic constraints.
4. Generated indexes support discovery but have no independent authority.
5. Independently documented systems retain authority over their internal domain model and behavior.
6. Missing information is not inferred from obsolete documents or undeclared compatibility behavior.

AI-assisted work starts at [`docs/AI_CONTEXT.md`](docs/AI_CONTEXT.md).

## Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         user surfaces                            │
│ local work • guidance • private instructions • offline learning │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│             optional kOA Spaces experience layer                 │
│ module selector • sidebar • top bar • shared page surface       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                 profile-selected kOA systems                     │
│ Ariane • Konnaxion • Orgo • Kristal • language runtimes         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    internal kOA components                       │
│ node • governance • trust • audit • resources • publication     │
│ kOA Mediatheque: private, local, offline authority              │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│               governed external interchange                     │
│ publish_to_uckk • import_from_uckk • receipts • provenance      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│         UCKK: online Moodle learning and dissemination          │
│ courses • learning paths • instructions • UCKK Mediatheque      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## kOA Spaces experience layer

kOA Spaces is an independently documented, optional subsystem integrated by kOA-Linux as the global experience and navigation layer.

It owns:

- the module selector;
- the active-module sidebar;
- global top-bar composition;
- the shared page surface and presentation routing;
- responsive and accessibility behavior of the global shell;
- offline presentation state;
- validation and atomic activation of Space definitions and interface manifests.

It does not own:

- authentication or authorization;
- business workflows or domain state;
- media, learning, task, governance, or publication authority;
- release signing or host-level activation authority;
- privileged host operations;
- resource admission or scheduling;
- backup, restore, or disaster recovery;
- the internal implementation of Ariane, Konnaxion, Orgo, SenTient, SemantiK Architect, or another contributing system.

A route, menu item, alias, sidebar entry, or widget is a presentation contribution only. Every operation remains authorized and executed by the system that owns the underlying capability and state. Removing kOA Spaces removes that presentation surface without transferring or deleting the authoritative state of contributing systems.

Canonical entry points:

- [`docs/02-system/21-koa-spaces-experience-layer.md`](docs/02-system/21-koa-spaces-experience-layer.md);
- [`docs/02-system/22-koa-spaces-interface-composition.md`](docs/02-system/22-koa-spaces-interface-composition.md);
- [`docs/03-profiles/14-koa-spaces-deployment.md`](docs/03-profiles/14-koa-spaces-deployment.md);
- [`docs/04-components/subsystems/koa-spaces.md`](docs/04-components/subsystems/koa-spaces.md);
- [`docs/contracts/subsystems/koa-spaces.subsystem.json`](docs/contracts/subsystems/koa-spaces.subsystem.json).

## The two Mediatheques

The **kOA Mediatheque** and the **UCKK Mediatheque** use the same shared Mediatheque frame or compatible versions of it. The frame covers object identity, versions, hashes, metadata, dimensions, collections, relationships, rights, restrictions, provenance, renditions, lifecycle, manifests, and receipts.

They remain distinct authorities:

| Surface | Primary role | Connectivity | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **kOA Mediatheque** | Private local files, instructions, organizational knowledge, downloaded learning material, and offline use | Fully local and offline-capable | Owns local records, local versions, storage bindings, local rights state, and local lifecycle |
| **UCKK Mediatheque** | Online educational distribution inside UCKK/Moodle | Online platform | Owns UCKK records, courses, paths, activities, permissions, and online lifecycle |

A common frame does not create a shared database, shared identifier space, shared access control, shared lifecycle, or automatic synchronization.

## Governed UCKK interchange

kOA-Linux exposes two explicit operations:

```text
publish_to_uckk
import_from_uckk
```

### Local to online

```text
local selection
→ rights, consent, and disclosure review
→ Publication Gateway authorization
→ UCKK-specific package and transport
→ UCKK acceptance
→ local publication receipt
```

The kOA source remains authoritative locally. UCKK creates or updates a separate online object and becomes authoritative for that remote object.

### Online to local

```text
UCKK course, path, instruction, or resource selection
→ source, license, integrity, and compatibility verification
→ controlled download or offline bundle transfer
→ quarantine and validation
→ explicit acceptance by the kOA Mediatheque
→ local offline availability with preserved UCKK provenance
```

The imported copy becomes a local kOA object. It does not grant kOA write authority over the UCKK source.

No background bidirectional synchronization is implied. Each direction has its own request, validation, receipt, failure state, and conflict policy.

## Offline learning and private instruction

A deployment can use kOA-Linux as a private operational library or as an offline learning environment. It may contain:

- the complete kOA-Linux user and administrator manual;
- procedures for one organization;
- a school curriculum for an isolated community;
- maintenance and emergency instructions;
- a local professional training program;
- an “univers-cité” devoted to bread making, agriculture, construction, health, or another practical domain.

An installation is not required to accept a universal public catalog. It can keep all locally authored content private. Selected UCKK courses and learning paths can be downloaded, verified, retained locally, and consulted for long periods without Internet access.

## Internal kOA components

Internal components documented completely by kOA include:

- `koa_node_agent`;
- `governance_policy_runtime`;
- `identity_and_trust`;
- `audit_broker`;
- `publication_gateway`;
- `resource_governor`;
- `kristal_runtime`;
- `koa_mediatheque`.

UCKK is not an internal kOA-Linux component and is not required for local or offline operation.

## Independently documented systems

Ariane, kOA Spaces, Konnaxion, Orgo, SenTient, and SemantiK Architect retain authority over their internal behavior. kOA boundary summaries live under [`docs/04-components/subsystems/`](docs/04-components/subsystems/), and their machine-readable boundary contracts live under [`docs/contracts/subsystems/`](docs/contracts/subsystems/). kOA Spaces is integrated only as the optional navigation and interface-composition layer; its presence does not make presentation artifacts authoritative.

UCKK is handled as an external online Moodle integration rather than as a mounted local subsystem.

## Foundational principles

1. **Offline continuity** — installed local capabilities and content remain usable without permanent connectivity.
2. **Explicit authority** — every mutation, import, publication, activation, or privilege use has a resolvable owner and authorization path.
3. **Component separation** — common schemas and shared infrastructure do not merge authority.
4. **Safe degradation** — unavailable external services disable only their dependent operations.
5. **Verified transitions** — imported bundles, publications, releases, restores, and critical mutations produce structured evidence.
6. **Deterministic-first operation** — core local behavior is reproducible; AI remains optional and non-authoritative.
7. **Selective disclosure** — private local content is not transferred merely because a compatible online destination exists.
8. **Portability and exit** — export, transfer, restore, self-hosting, and independent consumption remain testable capabilities.
9. **Replaceable experience layer** — kOA Spaces may be disabled or replaced without transferring authority, deleting business state, or disabling native administration and subsystem interfaces.

# Release locks

This source directory intentionally contains no hand-maintained lock files. Release locks are deterministic build outputs emitted under `generated/release/locks/` by `koa_assembly.releases.locks`.

A lock binds exact channel release identities, artifact identities, versions, manifest references, integrity values, source digests, compatibility evidence, signature references, provenance references, and recovery declarations. A lock is immutable once published. A changed input produces a new lock identity; it never mutates an existing lock in place.

Lock generation MUST fail closed when:

- a canonical channel is missing or duplicated;
- an artifact has unknown or multiple channel membership;
- a mutable tag or implicit `latest` selection is supplied;
- an artifact, source, manifest, signature, provenance, SBOM, or evidence reference is unresolved;
- required cross-channel compatibility is not `tested_compatible`;
- rollback or forward-repair material is absent.

Locks are evidence inputs and deployment constraints. They do not publish or activate artifacts, change component authority, or replace the signed Release Set manifest.

FILE: release/README.md
AUTHORITY: canonical
================================================================================================

# kOA release construction

This directory defines implementation settings and source templates for release construction. It does not own release-channel identity, artifact-class membership, signing authority, or activation authority.

Canonical ownership remains with:

- `docs/contracts/release-channels.contract.json` for the four channel identities and membership rules;
- `docs/contracts/artifact-classes.contract.json` for artifact classes and class lifecycle behavior;
- `docs/contracts/artifact-contracts/release-set.schema.json` for Release Set structure;
- profile, component, security, and lifecycle contracts for target-specific compatibility and activation boundaries.

## Four independent channels

| Source settings | Canonical channel | Namespace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channels/os-image.toml` | `system` | `koa.system` |
| `channels/service-bundle.toml` | `services` | `koa.services` |
| `channels/governance-policy.toml` | `governance` | `koa.governance` |
| `channels/kristal-artifacts.toml` | `knowledge` | `koa.knowledge` |

Versions are independent. Activation is not. Every activation candidate MUST bind exactly one release from all four channels in a signed Release Set whose compatibility status is `tested_compatible`. Matching versions or selecting the newest release never proves compatibility.

The settings files deliberately do not duplicate artifact-class membership. The assembler resolves membership from the canonical registries and blocks unknown, omitted, or multiply assigned artifacts.

## Construction boundary

`koa_assembly.releases.manifest` and `koa_assembly.releases.locks` consume canonical contracts, package manifests, profile selections, exact artifact identities, validation evidence, signatures, provenance, SBOM references, and recovery declarations. They write deterministic outputs only under `generated/release/`.

The templates in `manifests/` are non-authoritative candidate skeletons. A generator MUST replace every `replace.*` identity and reference, recompute integrity data, validate the result against the applicable canonical schema, and reject unresolved placeholders before publication.

Publication, distribution, installation, staging, and activation are separate states. Neither a manifest nor a lock activates content. Activation remains an explicit, target-scoped, owner-controlled, receipted transition.

## Prerequisites

End-to-end generation depends on the assembly release-set/lock/manifest implementation and the offline-bundle/repository implementation. Their absence MUST produce a blocked result; this directory does not provide fallback implementations. Signing, verification, SBOM, provenance, promotion, and rollback are defined by later release bundles.

# Security Policy

## Supported releases

Security support applies only to a complete, signed, verified Release Set whose lifecycle status and support decision are active in the canonical release records.

This greenfield repository snapshot does not declare a published runtime Release Set. Source branches, pull requests, development artifacts, unsigned packages, incomplete channel combinations, and unverified offline bundles are not supported releases merely because they are available.

When release infrastructure is present, support status must be derived from the active release contracts and records, not from this file, a branch name, a mutable tag, or a directory name.

## Report a vulnerability privately

Do not open a public issue for a suspected vulnerability.

Use the repository host's private security-reporting feature when it is enabled. If no private reporting feature is available, contact the maintainers through an already established private project channel. The supplied authority does not declare a public security email address, so this file does not invent one.

Do not include production credentials, private keys, access tokens, personal data, decrypted recovery material, or unnecessary governed content. Provide minimized evidence sufficient to reproduce and assess the issue.

A useful report includes:

- affected component, integration, profile, artifact, or release identity;
- exact version, commit, digest, or Release Set reference;
- deployment profile and relevant operating mode;
- impact and prerequisites;
- reproducible steps or a minimal proof of concept;
- observed and expected behavior;
- relevant logs with secrets and governed payloads removed;
- any known containment or recovery action.

## Handling process

Maintainers should:

1. acknowledge the private report through the same private channel;
2. establish the affected authority owner and scope;
3. preserve evidence without broadening disclosure;
4. classify whether the issue affects source, build, artifact, release, activation, runtime, recovery, or trust state;
5. reproduce the issue in an isolated environment using non-production identities and data;
6. prepare a bounded correction, validation plan, and rollback or forward-repair path;
7. publish updated artifacts, evidence, revocation information, or operational guidance through the governed release process when required;
8. coordinate public disclosure only after affected users have an actionable protected path.

No response-time promise is declared by the supplied authority. Reporters must not interpret silence as permission to disclose secrets or exploit production systems.

## Scope priorities

Reports are especially relevant when they concern:

- identity, trust roots, signatures, key custody, or revocation;
- privilege boundaries, broker operations, path traversal, sandboxing, capabilities, seccomp, LSM, or polkit;
- cross-component data access or authority transfer;
- release, update, offline import, activation, rollback, restore, or recovery integrity;
- secret exposure, privacy, selective audit, or support-bundle redaction;
- external integration boundaries or unaccepted candidate content;
- resource-exhaustion behavior that can bypass declared limits;
- generated-content, dependency, source-pin, or provenance substitution.

## Safe research expectations

Do not access data or systems beyond the authorization provided to you. Do not cause persistent service disruption, alter authoritative data, weaken trust state, or retain secrets. Stop testing when continued activity could affect users or production authority.

This policy is operational guidance. Canonical security controls and release requirements remain in the contracts and owning normative documents under `docs/`.

# Contract fixtures and tests

This directory contains deterministic repository-level contract tests. The suite validates:

- the exact inventories and stable identities of component, subsystem, and profile contracts;
- the four independent release channels and a minimal valid Release Set;
- all artifact-contract JSON Schemas as Draft 2020-12 schemas;
- a minimal valid offline bundle;
- the public Python bindings and, when B-0014 through B-0016 are present, every binding payload against its dependency-owned schema.

## Fixtures

- `minimal-profile-plan.json` is a deterministic discovery fixture. It is not a new profile authority.
- `minimal-release-set.json` validates against `release-set.schema.json`.
- `offline-bundle.json` validates against `offline-bundle.schema.json`.
- `invalid-signature.json` is intentionally invalid only because `verification_status` is outside the schema enum. The test asserts that exact failure path and keyword.

## Running

```sh
PYTHONPATH=interfaces/python/src pytest -q tests/contracts
```

The tests perform no network access and do not mutate repository files. A missing dependency schema is reported as an explicit skip only in the binding-to-schema test; it becomes executable automatically when the dependency bundle is integrated.

FILE: tools/README.md
AUTHORITY: canonical
================================================================================================

# kOA repository tooling

`tools/` contains the local, non-privileged command surface used to validate,
generate, assemble, test, diagnose, build, verify, and release declared kOA
artifacts. It orchestrates canonical implementations; it does not own component
policy, profile composition, release authority, or privileged host operations.

The source layout and path ownership are defined by:

- `docs/02-system/code-and-filesystem-architecture/31-operations-tests-tools-development-and-ci.md`;
- `docs/02-system/code-and-filesystem-architecture/33-path-ownership-and-change-rules.md`;
- `docs/contracts/toolchains/python-uv.toolchain.json`;
- `docs/05-development/14-build-test-and-validation.md`.

## Prerequisites

The active development profile must provide `python`, `uv`, and `git`. The
workspace root must already contain the version-controlled files
`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `.python-version`, and `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
The scripts never download or install UV through a remote shell script and
never refresh dependency resolution implicitly.

Each branch or worktree owns its own `.venv`. A content-addressed UV download
cache may be shared, but a mutable installed environment must not be shared.

## Bootstrap

Linux or WSL:

```console
./tools/scripts/bootstrap.sh
./tools/scripts/bootstrap.sh --offline
```

PowerShell:

```powershell
./tools/scripts/bootstrap.ps1
./tools/scripts/bootstrap.ps1 -Offline
```

Bootstrap is idempotent. It performs exactly these locked operations:

1. verify `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, and `.python-version`;
2. require profile-provided `python` and `uv`;
3. run `uv lock --check`;
4. run `uv sync --frozen --all-groups`, with `UV_OFFLINE=1` in offline mode.

An unavailable prerequisite or missing workspace marker exits explicitly. The
script does not repair a lock, select an undeclared index, or fall back to a
global Python environment.

## Development setup

Linux or WSL:

```console
./tools/scripts/setup-development.sh
```

PowerShell:

```powershell
./tools/scripts/setup-development.ps1
```

The setup script runs bootstrap, installs the repository-local pre-commit hook
through the frozen UV environment, and verifies the CLI help surface. Repeated
execution updates the same hook and synchronized environment rather than
creating parallel mutable state.

## Root CLI

The package entry point is `koa_tools.cli:main`. Until the root project exposes
the console script, the equivalent source invocation is:

```console
uv run --frozen python -m koa_tools.cli --help
```

The root help and command catalog are stable and do not import command modules.
The closed catalog is:

- `validate`;
- `generate`;
- `assemble`;
- `build-image`;
- `build-bundle`;
- `verify`;
- `test`;
- `release`;
- `diagnose`.

Root options must precede the command. `--repository-root PATH` may select an
explicit workspace root; otherwise the CLI searches upward from the current
working directory for all three canonical Python root markers.

A command module must expose this interface:

```text
main(argv: tuple[str, ...], *, repository_root: Path) -> int
```

Command modules return an integer exit code from 0 through 255. A catalogued
command whose implementation is absent exits with code 69. Invalid root CLI
arguments exit with code 2, an unexpected software defect exits with code 70,
and an interrupted command exits with code 130. No missing command is reported
as successful.

## Process execution API

`koa_tools.process.run_process` executes an argument vector without a shell,
uses a declared working directory, captures UTF-8 output, supports bounded
execution, and raises typed exceptions for start, timeout, and non-zero-exit
failures.

```python
from koa_tools.process import run_process

result = run_process(
    ["uv", "lock", "--check"],
    cwd=repository_root,
    timeout=120,
)
```

Do not pass secrets in command-line arguments. Secrets must enter a child
process only through an approved injected environment or broker. The process
API does not log environment values.

## Focused validation

From a synchronized workspace:

```console
uv run --frozen python -m compileall tools/src/koa_tools
uv run --frozen pytest tools/tests/test_cli.py
bash -n tools/scripts/bootstrap.sh tools/scripts/setup-development.sh
python docs/tools/check_greenfield_architecture.py
python docs/tools/validate_docs.py
```

Local success is workspace feedback, not release-authoritative evidence.

# About This Wiki

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

## Two reading paths

### Main — what it does

The main path explains the social and operational purpose of the ecosystem: knowledge, learning, deliberation, judgment, execution, memory, culture, language, autonomy, and collective capacity.

### Technical reference — how kOA-Linux supports it

The technical path summarizes profiles, components, trust, lifecycle, security, operations, contracts, and conformance.

## Duplication rule

This Wiki should explain the role of independent products but not recreate their internal documentation. Konnaxion, Orgo, SemantiK Architect, Kristal, SenTient, and other systems keep their own repositories or Wikis. This Wiki links to them and documents only the kOA-Linux boundary.

## Authority

The Wiki is explanatory. Repository contracts, accepted decisions, normative source documents, generated catalogs, and validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux. Product Wikis remain authoritative for their own product-level explanations.

# AI and External Integrations

> **Authority notice:** This wiki is a readable navigation layer. Source contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators in the repository remain authoritative.

## Baseline rule

AI is optional, capability-scoped, attributable, and unable to create invisible authority. Core operation remains deterministic and does not require native generative AI.

External outputs remain non-authoritative unless an explicit review and admission process transfers accepted facts into an authoritative owner.

- explicit user or system authorization;
- declared capability and data scope;
- no silent provider substitution;

# AI Assistance and Automation

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## AI is optional capability, not hidden authority

kOA-Linux Operating System may expose local or external AI services for search assistance, summarization, classification, drafting, reconciliation, translation support or interface guidance. Those services do not automatically become authoritative sources of facts, policy, permissions or system state.

## Allowed roles

Depending on policy, an AI system may:

- propose classifications or candidate entities;
- summarize selected material with source links;
- draft text for human review;
- recommend a navigation path;
- suggest tasks or routing;
- assist multilingual work where deterministic resources are unavailable;
- identify patterns for review.

## Prohibited shortcuts

An AI service must not silently:

- invent missing architectural authority;
- convert a candidate claim into a validated fact;
- approve its own output;
- bypass consent or disclosure limits;
- gain unrestricted filesystem, database or host access;
- replace a missing subsystem with an undeclared provider;
- execute a sensitive action without the required task, policy and authorization chain.

## Automation as accountable work

Automated activity should be represented as tasks or declared operations with an actor identity, input references, capability restrictions, resource limits, expected output, status, evidence and failure code.

## External services

When data leaves the local environment, the user and policy layer need to know what is sent, to whom, for which purpose, under which retention assumptions, and whether a local alternative exists.

## Sources

- [docs/02-system/09-ai-boundary.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/09-ai-boundary.md)
- [docs/02-system/10-external-ai-surfaces.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/10-external-ai-surfaces.md)
- [docs/07-security/11-ai-boundaries.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/07-security/11-ai-boundaries.md)

# Ariane

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

Ariane represents interfaces, controls, actions, states, and relationships as a semantic navigation graph. It supports intent-based guidance, accessibility, and bounded automation without conflating navigation with authorization.

Use the [public Ariane overview](https://initkoa.org/technology/ariane) and [Assisted Navigation with Ariane](Assisted-Navigation-with-Ariane).

kOA-Linux provides local runtime, profile selection, permissions, resources, and optional external voice boundaries.

FILE: wiki/Assisted-Navigation-with-Ariane.md

<!-- Explanatory wiki projection; not an independent normative authority. -->

# Assisted Navigation with Ariane

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## What Ariane changes

Traditional automation sees an interface as pixels, coordinates, selectors or undocumented scripts. Ariane treats the interface as data: screens, controls, actions, states and relationships form a semantic graph.

That graph allows a person, an assistive technology, or a bounded agent to ask not only “where is the button?” but “what action is available, what does it do, what state is required, and what happens next?”

## Navigation by intention

```text
user intention
    ↓
permitted capability and current context
    ↓
Ariane interface graph
    ↓
possible actions and prerequisites
    ↓
guided step, assistive action or bounded automation
    ↓
visible result and receipt when required
```

## Use cases

- guide a user through a complex administrative process;
- expose software to screen readers and other assistive systems through semantic actions;
- provide consistent navigation across profile-specific interfaces;
- help a local agent locate a permitted control without unrestricted host access;
- support multilingual labels while preserving one underlying action model;
- record which action was requested and which interface transition occurred.

## Boundaries

Ariane describes navigation and interaction possibilities. It does not automatically authorize an action. Authorization, consent, data disclosure and host privilege remain separate decisions.

External voice or AI services are optional integrations. The local navigation model remains distinct from any provider and must degrade explicitly when an optional service is unavailable.

## Offline behavior

The local graph and approved interface metadata can remain usable without network access. Remote voice recognition or remote language services may be unavailable, but their absence must not silently change the action model.

## Sources

- [Ariane public overview](https://initkoa.org/technology/ariane)
- [docs/02-system/11-ariane-system-boundary.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/11-ariane-system-boundary.md)
- [docs/10-adrs/ADR-021-ariane-local-navigation-with-optional-external-voice.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/10-adrs/ADR-021-ariane-local-navigation-with-optional-external-voice.md)
- [docs/contracts/subsystems/ariane.subsystem.json](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/contracts/subsystems/ariane.subsystem.json)

# Authority and Documentation

> **Authority notice:** This wiki is a readable navigation layer. Source contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators in the repository remain authoritative.

## Contract-first architecture

The documentation system is contract-first. Source contracts and focused explanatory documents own facts. Catalogs, indexes, matrices, manifests, and AI context packages are generated projections.

## Authority order

| Layer | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Accepted decisions | Close significant architectural choices |
| Source contracts | Own machine-readable system, component, profile, subsystem-boundary, integration, toolchain, and artifact facts |
| Normative source documents | Explain requirements and procedures within their declared scope |
| Executable validators | Enforce identities, schemas, references, boundaries, generated consistency, and release gates |
| Generated outputs | Support discovery only; never override a source |
| Recipes and examples | Provide bounded non-authoritative implementation guidance |

## Scope discipline

Authority remains explicit across global, profile, component, subsystem-boundary, integration, artifact, and recipe scopes. A narrower source cannot silently become global.

## Subsystem authority

Mounted subsystem documentation owns internal product behavior. kOA boundary contracts own deployment, resources, lifecycle, trust, health, storage exposure, artifact admission, and cross-subsystem interactions.

Missing, conflicting, or unresolved authority blocks the affected activation. No undeclared replacement is selected.

## Generated navigation

Generated files under `docs/generated/` are disposable and rebuildable. Do not edit them manually.

```bash
python docs/tools/build_indexes.py
python docs/tools/build_ai_context.py
python docs/tools/check_generated_content.py
```

## AI reading order

1. [`docs/AI_CONTEXT.md`](../blob/main/docs/AI_CONTEXT.md)
2. [`docs/contracts/ai-navigation.contract.json`](../blob/main/docs/contracts/ai-navigation.contract.json)
3. applicable source contract;
4. applicable kOA boundary page;
5. mounted subsystem documentation when internal behavior is needed;
6. generated indexes for discovery only.

## Sources

- [`docs/00-governance/00-documentation-architecture.md`](../blob/main/docs/00-governance/00-documentation-architecture.md)
- [`docs/00-governance/01-authority.md`](../blob/main/docs/00-governance/01-authority.md)

# Capability Status

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## Status vocabulary

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Publicly described | The capability is described on initkoa.org or an official public context pack. |
| Boundary specified | The kOA-Linux repository defines how the subsystem integrates or operates. |
| Target architecture | The required behavior is specified but needs implementation evidence. |
| Profile-dependent | Availability depends on the selected deployment profile and installed artifacts. |
| Experimental | The public source explicitly presents the system or feature as conceptual or experimental. |

## Capability matrix

| Capability | Public description | kOA-Linux boundary | Production claim |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Siloed sovereign operation | System-of-systems and offline/portable architecture | Strongly specified | Requires deployment evidence |
| Kristal portable knowledge | Core public technology | Runtime and artifact lifecycle specified | Requires implementation and conformance evidence |
| Ariane assisted navigation | Public technology | Local boundary and optional external voice ADR | Requires subsystem implementation evidence |
| Orgo roles, tasks and closure | Core public platform | Subsystem boundary specified | Requires Orgo deployment evidence |
| Konnaxion public coordination | Core public platform | Subsystem boundary specified | Requires Konnaxion deployment evidence |
| Multilingual deterministic rendering | Publicly described | Language boundary and artifact lifecycle specified | Semantik Architect is still described as experimental |
| SenTient reconciliation | Public conceptual architecture | Optional isolated boundary | Explicitly not production-ready |
| Offline operation | Core design commitment | Profiles, operations and lifecycle specified | Must be tested per profile |
| Collective governance to execution | Cross-system design | Governance and boundary components specified | End-to-end integration evidence required |

<!-- Explanatory wiki projection; not an independent normative authority. -->

# Collective Intelligence to Governance

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## The objective

Collective intelligence is useful only when it improves understanding without hiding legitimacy. Governance becomes operational only when accepted outcomes can be converted into bounded authority, responsibilities, tasks, deadlines, review and recourse.

## Konnaxion's role

Konnaxion supports learning, structured deliberation, proposals, argument, drafting and collective decision interfaces. Kollective Intelligence can expose multiple transparent readings of a decision while keeping the democratic baseline visible.

Smart Vote and EkoH-style readings may show domain-bounded competence signals. They are advisory views unless an explicit constitutional rule grants a specific effect. They do not silently reallocate decision rights.

## Governance layer

The governance layer evaluates:

- which procedure applies;
- whether quorum or thresholds are satisfied;
- which authority recognizes the result;
- what scope and duration the decision has;
- which rights, consent or disclosure limits apply;
- how the decision can be contested, reviewed or revoked;
- whether the result may produce a mandate or operational authorization.

## Orgo's role

Orgo turns an accepted outcome into accountable work:

```text
decision or mandate
    ↓
responsible function or role
    ↓
case and tasks
    ↓
response windows and escalation
    ↓
explicit closure and evidence
    ↓
review and institutional learning
```

## Critical separation

A vote or collective reading does not directly become root access, a signing key, a database write or an unbounded automated action. Policy evaluation, authorization and technical privilege remain separate boundaries.

- [Kollective Intelligence](https://initkoa.org/platforms/konnaxion/kollective-intelligence)
- [Smart Vote](https://initkoa.org/platforms/konnaxion/kollective-intelligence/smart-vote)
- [EkoH](https://initkoa.org/initiatives/civic-governance/constitution/ekoh)
- [Civic Constitution](https://initkoa.org/initiatives/civic-governance/constitution)
- [docs/02-system/15-governance-policy-runtime.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/15-governance-policy-runtime.md)

## Intended environment

A community deployment uses Konnaxion for learning, projects, deliberation, collective decisions, distribution and shared memory, while kOA-Linux provides local continuity, trust and separation from private operational data.

# Constitutional Principles

> **Authority notice:** This wiki is a readable navigation layer. Source contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators in the repository remain authoritative.

## Global commitments

1. **Offline capability** — Core consultation, verification, execution, and recovery remain available without permanent cloud connectivity.
2. **Verified activation** — Artifacts, policies, services, and releases activate only after integrity, compatibility, trust, and authorization checks succeed.
3. **Safe degradation** — Failures block unsafe actions while preserving context, status, evidence, and recoverability.
4. **Deterministic-first execution** — Core transformations are reproducible; AI remains optional, bounded, attributable, and unable to create invisible authority.
5. **Least privilege** — Integrated subsystems and optional services do not receive unrestricted host capabilities.
6. **Explicit governance** — Governance rules are versioned policy artifacts rather than undocumented operator behavior.
7. **Selective audit** — The system remains auditable without indiscriminate disclosure of personal or operational data.
8. **Semantic sovereignty** — Terminology, authority channels, contested concepts, and multilingual mappings remain governed and portable.
9. **Cultural rights enforcement** — Consent, community authority, access conditions, withdrawal, and AI restrictions are enforced across the data lifecycle.
10. **Credible exit** — Export, transfer, restore, self-hosting, trust handover, and operator independence are tested capabilities.

## Interpretation

Profiles and overlays may strengthen or narrow implementation choices, but they do not weaken global constitutional requirements. Components define behavior only inside active system, profile, security, lifecycle, data-ownership, and integration boundaries.

# Contributing

> **Authority notice:** This wiki is a readable navigation layer. Source contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators in the repository remain authoritative.

## Documentation change sequence

1. Update the authoritative source contract or normative source document.
2. When the change belongs to an independent subsystem, update its official documentation and only the kOA boundary in this repository.
3. Add or update an ADR when an architectural decision changes.
4. Rebuild generated indexes and AI context.
5. Run the complete validation pipeline.
6. Commit source changes and regenerated outputs together.
7. Update the wiki only when its navigation or explanatory summary changes.

## Prohibited documentation patterns

Do not:

- recreate hand-maintained registries or file catalogs;
- duplicate a subsystem's internal model, complete API, workflow, or user interface;
- edit generated outputs as sources;
- infer missing authority from historical material;
- introduce undeclared substitution or compatibility behavior;
- use `.lnk` files for subsystem documentation mounts;
- make an implementation claim without test and evidence support.

## Commands

```bash
python docs/tools/build_indexes.py
python docs/tools/build_ai_context.py
python docs/tools/validate_docs.py
```

# Control, Portability, and Recovery

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

Sovereignty requires practical control over data, meaning, software, trust, and continuity.

The architecture therefore treats the following as tested capabilities:

- export of local data, knowledge artifacts, media manifests, policies, cases, tasks, and evidence;
- verification of exported packages;
- restoration on another compatible node;
- backup and recovery without permanent cloud dependency;
- trust-root and operator handover;
- revocation of former access;
- visibility into active versions and queued exchanges;
- preservation of source authority when artifacts move between systems.

Portability does not mean that every external platform database is copied locally. It means that selected, governed artifacts can move while preserving identity, provenance, rights, versions, and authority boundaries.

# Crisis, Field, and Air-Gapped Use

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. ## Intended environment

A field team, crisis unit, remote institution or high-assurance environment may operate with intermittent or no network access. The deployment must preserve local knowledge, operational work, evidence and recovery without pretending that remote services are available.

- verified procedures and knowledge packs;
- local search and navigation;

- stale or unverified data remains visibly labeled;
- conflicts are reviewed under declared strategies;
- failed verification blocks activation;
- emergency or break-glass actions are bounded, logged and reviewed;
- offline does not remove accountability.

<!-- Explanatory wiki projection. Normative authority remains in the repository and subsystem documentation. -->

# Cultural Sovereignty

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

## Culture as governed memory

Cultural sovereignty requires more than a repository of files. A cultural system must preserve the relationships that make a work meaningful:

- creator and community identity;
- provenance and lineage;
- cultural context;
- rights, restrictions, licences, and attribution;
- consent and withdrawal;
- authority to interpret, display, reuse, translate, or train AI;
- moderation, disputes, revisions, and decision records.

## Kreative and Konservation

Within Konnaxion:

- **Kreative** is the cultural memory, collaboration, discovery, and creator-network layer.
- **Konservation** is the preservation and archive-oriented submodule.
- **Kontact** connects creators, communities, institutions, collaborators, patrons, and opportunities.

Detailed product documentation belongs in the [Konnaxion Wiki](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion/wiki), especially [Konservation](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion/wiki/Konservation) and [Kontact](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion/wiki/Kontact).

## Integration without appropriation

External collections can be mapped into shared structures while preserving source identity, stewardship, rights, and access restrictions. Interoperability must not erase the authority of museums, archives, Indigenous governance bodies, artists, or communities.

AI may suggest tags, descriptions, translations, accessibility text, or duplicate candidates. It must not silently define cultural meaning or override community authority.

# Current Scope and Limits

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## What is complete in this repository

The documentation corpus defines and validates a contract-first target architecture for kOA-Linux Operating System. It includes system principles, profiles, component boundaries, security, lifecycle, operations, conformance, schemas, accepted ADRs, generators and validators.

## What remains implementation-dependent

The repository does not prove that every component is already implemented or production-tested. Evidence is still required for final host distribution choices, immutable image mechanisms, production key custody, hardware assurance, capacity limits, database isolation at scale, regulatory profiles and production implementations of internal services.

## Subsystem dependency

The detailed user behavior of Ariane, Konnaxion, Orgo, SenTient, and SemantiK Architect belongs to those subsystem specifications. The kOA-Linux repository currently reserves documentation mount points for pinned official subsystem documentation.

## Public-site status distinctions

- Konnaxion, Orgo, Kristal and the governance model are described as core parts of the kOA ecosystem.
- Semantik Architect is described as an independent experimental architecture for deterministic multilingual rendering.
- SenTient is explicitly described as conceptual or experimental and not production-ready.
- The wiki therefore distinguishes **intended capability**, **specified boundary**, and **production evidence**.

## No silent completion claims

A validated documentation tree proves consistency of the documentation and contracts. It does not by itself prove performance, security, usability, legal compliance or operational readiness on every target deployment.

# From Decisions to Execution

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## Why decisions often fail

Many institutions can discuss and vote but cannot reliably convert an outcome into accountable follow-through. Responsibility remains implicit, deadlines disappear, and closure is replaced by status meetings or message threads.

Orgo supplies the execution layer, while kOA-Linux supplies the environment and governance boundary.

## Execution contract

An operationalized decision should identify:

- the decision or mandate reference;
- the responsible function or role;
- affected organizations, people or locations;
- required cases and tasks;
- inputs and expected outputs;
- response and completion windows;
- escalation rules;
- confidentiality and visibility;
- approval or human-review gates;
- closure criteria and evidence;
- review, appeal or revocation conditions.

## Signal-to-closure lifecycle

1. A decision, report, request or incident becomes a signal.
2. The signal is normalized and classified.
3. A case provides durable context and ownership.
4. Tasks express executable work.
5. Work routes to functions or roles rather than relying only on named individuals.
6. Time windows make delay visible.
7. Escalation occurs under explicit rules.
8. Closure records what happened and what remains open.
9. Patterns create review work.

## Automation

Tasks may be performed by humans, deterministic tools, constrained agents or hybrid methods. Automation must remain allowlisted, resource-bounded, attributable and subject to the same approval and evidence requirements.

## Sources

- [Orgo workflow](https://initkoa.org/platforms/orgo/workflow)
- [Orgo flows](https://initkoa.org/platforms/orgo/flows)
- [Routing and escalation](https://initkoa.org/platforms/orgo/routing-escalation)
- [Core guarantees](https://initkoa.org/platforms/orgo/guarantees)
- [docs/02-system/20-receipts-and-critical-transitions.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/20-receipts-and-critical-transitions.md)

# Deployment Choices

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## One architecture, different capability sets

kOA-Linux Operating System uses profiles to state what a deployment includes, how much resource it may consume, which network assumptions apply, and how it behaves when a capability is unavailable.

## Main choices

| Profile or overlay | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| User Lightweight | Daily local use on commodity hardware with bounded resources |
| Developer Linux Workstation | Isolated local development and testing on Linux |
| Developer Windows WSL | Isolated development from a Windows workstation using WSL |
| Sovereign Linux Node | Hardened production operation on one Linux node |
| Sovereign Hub | Locally autonomous shared services and coordination |
| Build Farm | Heavy compilation, validation, indexing, and artifact production |
| Control Plane | Release coordination, policy distribution, fleet metadata, and controlled oversight |
| Appliance Shell overlay | A focused appliance-style user surface |
| High Assurance overlay | Stronger trust, key custody, separation of duties, audit, and recovery requirements |
| Sovereign Offline overlay | Stricter offline and disconnected-operation conditions |

Profiles can compose with overlays, but an overlay may not silently weaken the primary profile's baseline.

| User Lightweight | primary | A resource-bounded, general-purpose Linux deployment for daily local use on commodity hardware. | [guide](../blob/main/docs/03-profiles/04-user-lightweight.md) | [contract](../blob/main/docs/contracts/profiles/user-lightweight.profile.json) |

## Composition rules

- Primary profiles establish the deployment baseline.
- Overlays add stricter or narrower conditions without silently weakening the baseline.
- Profile membership is explicit; components do not infer deployment from their own contracts.
- Resource, connectivity, security, offline, and degradation claims remain profile-scoped.

# Development Model

> **Authority notice:** This wiki is a readable navigation layer. Source contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators in the repository remain authoritative.

## Workspace isolation

A development workspace is the isolation unit for one application, branch, or worktree. Each workspace receives its own identity, mutable dependency environment, service state, ports, secrets, databases, volumes, and resource budget.

Shared content-addressed download and build caches may be reused. Mutable installed environments and runtime state are not shared.

## Python toolchain

UV is the declared Python dependency and environment manager. Workspaces use versioned `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` files with a workspace-local virtual environment.

## Service isolation

- rootless service containers where applicable;
- workspace-specific networks, sockets, volumes, and databases;
- explicit port allocation;
- no shared mutable secrets or application state;
- bounded CPU, memory, I/O, queues, and concurrency.

## Publication boundary

Development output is a candidate until it passes build, test, schema, provenance, evidence, and release admission controls. A local workspace cannot directly activate a production artifact.

# Education and Learning

# Everyday Use

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

A person does not interact with the entire architecture at once. They enter through the workspace relevant to their role and purpose.

Examples:

- learn from local or shared resources;
- navigate a complex process with Ariane assistance;
- join a Konnaxion project, consultation, debate, or cultural space;
- inspect the evidence and provenance behind a claim;
- see baseline and advisory readings of collective support;
- receive an Orgo task because a decision or signal requires action;
- work offline with local knowledge, files, and queued updates;
- preserve or publish selected cultural and educational content under explicit rights.

The interface should always show which organization, authority, profile, version, connectivity state, and next responsibility apply.

# Frequently Asked Questions

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

## Is kOA-Linux the whole kOA ecosystem?

No. kOA-Linux is the sovereign runtime. The wider ecosystem includes independently documented platforms, modules, knowledge systems, language systems, governance services, and cultural layers.

## Where are Konnaxion's modules documented?

In the [Konnaxion Wiki](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion/wiki). This Wiki lists the modules only to show how they fit into the knowledge-to-action loop.

## Where is Orgo documented?

In the [Orgo Wiki](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Orgo/wiki).

## Is collective intelligence the same as majority rule?

No. The architecture distinguishes equal political standing, advisory credibility, expertise signals, decision procedures, and technical authorization.

## Does kOA require consensus?

No. It aims to make disagreement structured, visible, and actionable while preserving minority positions, uncertainty, and recourse.

## Is UCKK part of kOA-Linux?

No. UCKK is an external Moodle platform. The kOA Mediatheque is the local media authority.

## Can the system work offline?

Yes, for profile-selected capabilities and artifacts present locally. External exchange and remote services are deferred or unavailable explicitly.

## Does AI decide?

No. AI may assist with extraction, summaries, translation, classification, or routing. Authoritative acceptance and sensitive actions remain governed.

## Does a passing documentation validation prove production readiness?

No. It proves the checks implemented for the documentation corpus. Runtime and deployment evidence remain separate.

# Files, Media, and Provenance

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

## Local authority

The **kOA Mediatheque** owns media and file records held by the local installation: identity, version, verified hash, managed content reference, metadata, provenance, rights, restrictions, relations, collections, languages, renditions, lifecycle, import/export history, backup, and restore state.

## Cultural context

Konnaxion's Kreative and Konservation layers add cultural context, creator and community authority, consent, exhibitions, collaboration, and rights-aware discovery. They should link to local media records rather than silently replace their authority.

## External UCKK objects

An object published to UCKK becomes a distinct UCKK object. A resource imported from UCKK becomes a distinct local kOA object. Provenance relates the records without merging databases or lifecycles.

## AI boundary

AI may propose tags, descriptions, translations, accessibility text, or duplicate candidates. The owning workflow accepts, rejects, or corrects those candidates; AI does not silently define meaning, rights, or authority.

Repository sources:

- [kOA Mediatheque system boundary](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/12-koa-mediatheque-system-boundary.md)

# Global Communications and Distribution

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## Communication is part of coordination

The kOA model does not treat communication as an isolated chat feature. A communication may be public knowledge, an announcement, a request, an incident report, a decision, a task-generating signal, a distribution package or a synchronization event.

## Two complementary paths

### Konnaxion: public and community distribution

Konnaxion supports the publication and distribution of learning resources, knowledge, projects, deliberation, decisions and shared memory. Content may be delivered online, mirrored locally or packaged for offline use.

### Orgo: communications that require accountable action

Orgo can ingest email, forms, APIs, field notes, call logs, imported archives and other signals. Role inboxes map communication channels to functions. Workflow rules decide whether a signal opens a case, creates tasks, routes work, starts a timer or triggers escalation.

## A governed communication path

```text
message, report or event
    ↓
identity, consent and disclosure checks
    ↓
classification: information / request / update / decision / report / distribution
    ↓
public distribution or private organizational routing
    ↓
receipt, ownership, task or queued delivery
    ↓
response, escalation and closure when action is required
```

## Global does not mean centralized

Distribution can cross organizations and regions while each node preserves its own authority, storage and policy. Portable artifacts, local mirrors, asynchronous queues and explicit gateways reduce dependence on one global service.

## Automation boundaries

Automated messages must identify their source, applicable policy, target scope and whether action is expected. High-volume automation must be rate-limited and cannot bypass consent, visibility or role permissions.

## Sources

- [Konnaxion](https://initkoa.org/platforms/konnaxion)
- [What Orgo does](https://initkoa.org/platforms/orgo/what-it-does)
- [Routing and escalation](https://initkoa.org/platforms/orgo/routing-escalation)
- [docs/02-system/07-cross-component-communication.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/07-cross-component-communication.md)
- [docs/07-security/17-cross-domain-publication.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/07-security/17-cross-domain-publication.md)

# Glossary

> **Authority notice:** This wiki is a readable navigation layer. Source contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators in the repository remain authoritative.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Active authority | The currently activated source contracts, accepted decisions, normative documents, and validation rules for a declared scope. |
| Artifact | A versioned object admitted, verified, activated, transferred, retained, or removed through a declared lifecycle contract. |
| Boundary contract | A machine-readable declaration of responsibilities, exchanges, dependencies, health, resources, security, and prohibited behavior at an integration boundary. |
| Candidate output | Information produced by an optional workbench or external integration that has not been accepted by an authoritative owner. |
| Component | An internal kOA unit whose responsibilities, state, interfaces, failure behavior, and evidence obligations are fully documented by kOA. |
| Contract-first | A documentation model in which source contracts own machine-readable facts and generated indexes provide discovery. |
| Credible exit | The tested ability to export, transfer, restore, self-host, hand over trust, or leave an operator or provider. |
| Generated projection | A rebuildable catalog, index, matrix, manifest, or AI context package with no independent authority. |
| Profile | A deployable selection of capabilities, components, subsystems, resources, connectivity, security, and degradation behavior. |
| Receipt | A machine-readable record of a governed decision or critical transition, including identity, authority, inputs, outcome, and evidence references. |
| Release set | A compatible, verified selection of versioned release-channel artifacts activated together. |
| Safe degradation | Failure behavior that blocks unsafe actions while preserving context, state, evidence, and a declared recovery path. |
| Selective audit | Auditability controlled by purpose, policy, disclosure class, and recourse rather than unrestricted transparency. |
| Subsystem | An independently documented product integrated through a kOA operating and integration boundary. |
| Workspace | A development isolation unit with its own identity, mutable dependencies, services, state, ports, secrets, databases, and resource budget. |

The canonical vocabulary is owned by [`docs/contracts/terminology.contract.json`](../blob/main/docs/contracts/terminology.contract.json). The readable source glossary is [`docs/01-constitution/13-glossary.md`](../blob/main/docs/01-constitution/13-glossary.md).

# Governance Plane

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## Purpose

The governance plane turns explicit sociotechnical rules into inspectable decisions about authorization, disclosure, activation, consent, rights, emergency behavior, export and recourse.

## It does not do

A governance result does not directly become root privilege. The system separates civic legitimacy, organizational mandates, knowledge authority, service permissions, signing authority and host operations.

## Main outputs

- authorization or denial;
- disclosure and publication decisions;
- activation decisions;
- policy and version references;
- conditions and expiry;
- receipts and evidence links;
- recourse or review hooks.

# Governance, Trust, Rights, and Recourse

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## Governance as an operating constraint

Governance is not a decorative policy page. It defines which actions are legitimate, which data may be disclosed, who may authorize sensitive transitions, how decisions are recorded, and how people can contest or exit the system.

## Core safeguards

- **Non-domination:** operators and technical administrators do not receive unlimited civic or organizational authority.
- **Auditability:** important outcomes can be traced to inputs, rules and authorized roles.
- **Contestability:** decisions and automated outcomes expose a review path.
- **Fail-closed integrity:** failed verification blocks authority rather than silently weakening rules.
- **Selective disclosure:** institutions can be accountable without publishing every personal or operational detail.
- **Consent and cultural rights:** access, use, withdrawal and AI restrictions follow explicit policy.
- **Right to exit:** people and organizations can export data, rules and portable artifacts.

## Trust layers

The system separates:

- identity of people and services;
- role or mandate authority;
- artifact integrity and signer trust;
- recognition of knowledge assertions;
- permission to disclose data;
- authorization to perform an operation;
- host privilege.

One form of trust does not automatically grant the others.

## Receipts and recourse

Critical decisions and operations should produce machine-readable receipts that identify the policy, inputs, decision, actor, time and relevant evidence. Recourse may reopen a case, suspend an action, create a review task or activate an appeal procedure.

## Sources

- [Civic Constitution](https://initkoa.org/initiatives/civic-governance/constitution)
- [Civic Bill of Rights](https://initkoa.org/initiatives/civic-governance/constitution/rights)
- [docs/01-constitution/10-selective-audit-and-recourse.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/01-constitution/10-selective-audit-and-recourse.md)
- [docs/02-system/15-governance-policy-runtime.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/15-governance-policy-runtime.md)
- [docs/02-system/20-receipts-and-critical-transitions.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/20-receipts-and-critical-transitions.md)

# From Groups to Organizations

> **Authority and status:** This wiki is an explanatory navigation layer. The repository contracts, accepted ADRs, normative documents, and executable validators remain authoritative for kOA-Linux Operating System. Public initkoa.org pages explain the wider kOA ecosystem and the product capabilities provided by its independently documented subsystems.

## A cross-system outcome

“Turn a group of people into an organization” is not one button or one database table. It is a progression from shared attention to legitimate structure and accountable execution. In kOA, this outcome spans Konnaxion, governance rules and Orgo.

## The progression

### 1. Gather around a subject, place or need

Konnaxion provides spaces for learning, collaboration, projects, public discussion and shared resources.

### 2. Form a shared purpose

The group develops a mission, problem statement, proposal or project. Relevant knowledge can be packaged and cited through Kristal.

### 3. Make membership and participation visible

The group identifies participants, contribution rules, consent, rights and the scope of public or private information.

### 4. Establish legitimate rules

The group adopts a charter, decision procedure, delegation model and review process. Advisory expertise can inform decisions without silently replacing the democratic baseline.

### 5. Create operational structure

Orgo represents the organization, roles, permissions, teams, role inboxes, cases, tasks, response windows and escalation ladders.

### 6. Execute and learn

Accepted decisions become owned work. Outcomes, unresolved issues, audits and recurring patterns return to the collective for review.

## What the operating system contributes

kOA-Linux provides the separated public and private environments, identity and trust services, policy evaluation, local databases, messaging boundaries, artifact storage, offline operation, backup and recovery.

## What remains a product contract

The exact onboarding flow, legal status, membership lifecycle, voting rules, role taxonomy and dissolution procedure must be defined by Konnaxion, Orgo and governance specifications. The operating system must not invent those rules.

## Sources

- [Konnaxion](https://initkoa.org/platforms/konnaxion)
- [What Orgo does](https://initkoa.org/platforms/orgo/what-it-does)
- [Civic Constitution](https://initkoa.org/initiatives/civic-governance/constitution)
- [docs/02-system/04-component-boundaries.md](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kOA-Linux/blob/main/docs/02-system/04-component-boundaries.md)

# kOA-Linux Operating System

> **Reading model:** The main path explains what the kOA ecosystem enables. The technical reference explains how kOA-Linux hosts, isolates, verifies, and operates those capabilities. Product-specific details remain in each subsystem's own documentation.

> **kOA-Linux Operating System is the sovereign runtime for a wider knowledge-to-action ecosystem.**

## The big picture

Communities, schools, organizations, researchers, public institutions, and cultural networks often possess information, experience, and motivation but lack a reliable path from what they know to what they can do together.

The wider **kOA ecosystem** is designed to operate that path:

```text
Know → Choose → Act → Remember → Know better
```

In operational terms:

```text
signals, documents, experience, and cultural memory
→ structured and verifiable knowledge
→ learning, consultation, and deliberation
→ legitimate decisions with visible reasoning
→ roles, tasks, coordination, escalation, and closure
→ evidence, institutional memory, and renewed knowledge
```

The aim is not to build one giant application. kOA is a **system of systems**: each platform owns a distinct part of the cycle, while kOA-Linux provides local execution, isolation, offline continuity, trust, policy, resources, recovery, and controlled integration.

## What the ecosystem does

| Collective need | kOA capability |
| --- | --- |
| Turn fragmented information into reusable knowledge | Semantic processing, [Kristal artifacts](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kristal-framework), provenance, versions, uncertainty, and verification |
| Help people learn and build competence | [Konnaxion](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion/wiki) learning modules, portable resources, multilingual rendering, and offline packages |
| Make disagreement understandable | Structured consultation, argumentation, drafting, and visible decision procedures |
| Improve judgment without replacing democracy | EkoH credibility signals and Smart Vote advisory readings kept separate from sovereign results |
| Turn decisions into accountable action | [Orgo](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Orgo/wiki) Cases, Tasks, roles, routing, deadlines, escalation, closure, and operational memory |
| Help groups become durable organizations | Membership, purpose, governance, roles, workflows, responsibility, and review loops |
| Preserve culture with authority and context | Kreative and Konservation: provenance, consent, rights, community authority, exhibitions, and cultural memory |
| Work across languages and meanings | [SemantiK Architect](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/SemantiK_Architect), governed terminology, multilingual mappings, and semantic sovereignty |
| Reconcile unstructured information with semantic systems | [SenTient](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/SenTient) extraction, entity linking, structured review, and candidate knowledge |
| Navigate complex software by intention | [Ariane](Ariane) semantic interface graphs and assisted navigation |
| Preserve and exchange learning media | Local kOA media authority plus the operational [UCKK Mediatheque](https://uckk.org), under separate databases and authorities |
| Continue locally and offline | kOA-Linux profiles, local storage, verified artifacts, queued exchange, backup, and safe degradation |
| Deploy Konnaxion as a governed local service | [Konnaxion Capsule Manager](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion_Capsule_Manager) packaging, verification, deployment, backup, restore, and rollback |
| Keep AI subordinate to governed workflows | AI may assist extraction, translation, synthesis, or routing; it does not create invisible authority |

## Modules and systems

### Public knowledge and civic collaboration — Konnaxion

[Konnaxion](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion) is the commons-facing platform. Its modules cover learning, governance, innovation, culture, and collective intelligence:

- **KonnectED** — Knowledge, CertifiKation
- **Ethikos** — Korum, Konsultations
- **keenKonnect** — Konstruct, Stockage
- **Kreative** — Konservation, Kontact
- **Kollective Intelligence** — EkoH, Smart Vote

Use the [Konnaxion Wiki](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion/wiki) for detailed module and submodule documentation.

For packaging and governed local deployment, use the [Konnaxion Capsule Manager repository](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Konnaxion_Capsule_Manager).

### Organizational execution — Orgo

[Orgo](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Orgo) turns signals and decisions into Cases, Tasks, roles, routing, reactivity windows, escalation, closure, and recurring review.

Use the [Orgo Wiki](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/Orgo/wiki) for its complete organizational and operational model.

### Knowledge, semantics, and language

- **[Kristal Framework](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/kristal-framework)** — portable, status-aware knowledge artifacts with provenance, validation, versioning, and offline runtime packs.
- **[SenTient](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/SenTient)** — optional semantic reconciliation and structured-extraction workbench whose outputs remain candidates until accepted.
- **[SemantiK Architect](https://github.com/Rejean-McCormick/SemantiK_Architect)** — deterministic multilingual realization of structured meaning.
- **[Ariane](Ariane)** — semantic navigation and interaction orchestration inside the kOA environment.

See [Related Wikis and Documentation](Related-Wikis) for the public repositories and product-specific documentation. This Wiki presents their place in the ecosystem without duplicating their complete specifications.

### Media, learning resources, and provenance

The **kOA Mediatheque** provides local, private-by-default, offline-capable media authority. The **UCKK Mediatheque** provides the online learning and publication environment available at [uckk.org](https://uckk.org).

The UCKK Mediatheque is operational, but its source repository is not public at this time. The local and online Mediatheques use compatible descriptive frames while retaining separate databases, identities, authorities, and lifecycles.

See [UCKK Mediatheque and exchange boundary](UCKK-Mediatheque) for the two explicit operations:

```text
publish_to_uckk
import_from_uckk
```

### Sovereign operating environment — kOA-Linux

kOA-Linux is responsible for the conditions under which the ecosystem operates:

- local execution and deployment profiles;
- identity, trust, and isolation;
- verified activation and fail-closed integrity;
- policy enforcement and bounded privilege;
- resource limits and workload admission;
- offline continuity and safe degradation;
- backup, recovery, and rollback;
- audit boundaries and traceable transitions;
- controlled publication, import, and external integration.

It does not absorb the product authority of Konnaxion, Orgo, Kristal Framework, SenTient, SemantiK Architect, or other independently documented systems.

Only systems that belong to the documented kOA ecosystem are listed here. Other repositories under the same GitHub account are not automatically part of this architecture.

## Social and institutional purpose

kOA treats collective intelligence as infrastructure, not as an automatic wisdom of crowds. A group becomes capable when it can govern the passages between contribution, meaning, knowledge, choice, responsibility, action, and memory.

The design therefore emphasizes:

- democratic legitimacy without technocracy;
- semantic sovereignty and multilingual dignity;
- non-domination, contestability, portability, and exit;
- social cohesion through shared reference points rather than forced uniformity;
- cultural sovereignty through provenance, consent, rights, and community authority;
- durable institutional memory;
- global collaboration combined with local autonomy.
